statement.informal: The scalar Gaussian-conjugate Bayesian (Kalman) update is the minimum-mean-squared-error estimator -- proven from scratch in MachLib's Mathlib-free real-analysis base, ZERO new axioms, no measure theory. Model: prior X~N(mu,sig2), measurement Y=X+N with noise N~N(0,r2) independent (the joint density is a bare PRODUCT of two 1-D densities -- independence by construction, no bivariate Gaussian, no covariance matrix). Completing the square (jointDensity_conjugacy) factors the joint density as marginal Y~N(mu,sig2+r2) TIMES posterior X|Y=y ~ N(m(y),tau2), where m(y)=mu+K(y-mu), K=sig2/(sig2+r2) is the Kalman gain and tau2=sig2*r2/(sig2+r2) the posterior variance. The exponent identity reduces to the polynomial identity p^2 t(s+t)+(q-p)^2 s(s+t)=q^2 st+(ps+pt-sq)^2; the normalizers match because both sqrt(2pi*sig2)sqrt(2pi*r2) and sqrt(2pi(sig2+r2))sqrt(2pi*tau2) equal 2pi*sig*r. MMSE-optimality is then the parallel-axis theorem (S7) instantiated at the posterior: posterior_mean_mmse gives tau2 <= tau2+(c-m(y))^2 (the posterior mean minimizes the conditional MSE, min=tau2); optimalMSE_tendsto gives the posterior-mean estimator's total (unconditional) MSE = tau2 exactly; mse_lower_bound gives that no continuous estimator beats tau2 (window-by-window Riemann-integral monotonicity). The unconditional result uses the iterated-integral device: the inner x-integral is closed-form by parallel-axis, leaving a single 1-D outer y-integral -- NO 2-D integration. postMean_eq_kalman cross-checks the optimal gain against the pre-existing purely-algebraic kalman_gain. Honest scope: SCALAR state+measurement; 'any estimator' = any continuous phi:Real->Real (MachLib has no measurable-function type).
statement.formal_lean:
theorem posterior_mean_mmse (mu sig2 r2 y c : Real) :
    postVar sig2 r2 <= postVar sig2 r2 + (c - postMean mu sig2 r2 y) * (c - postMean mu sig2 r2 y) := ...

theorem optimalMSE_tendsto (mu sig2 r2 : Real) (hsig2 : 0 < sig2) (hr2 : 0 < r2) :
    <total MSE of the posterior-mean estimator tends to postVar sig2 r2> := ...

theorem jointDensity_conjugacy (mu sig2 r2 x y : Real) (hsig2 : 0 < sig2) (hr2 : 0 < r2) :
    jointDensity mu sig2 r2 x y
      = gaussianDensity mu (margVar sig2 r2) y * gaussianDensity (postMean mu sig2 r2 y) (postVar sig2 r2) x := ...

common_mistakes.tactic: direct mach_mpoly on the cleared exponent identity in (x,mu,y) form
common_mistakes.why_fails: The subtractions (x-mu),(y-x),(y-mu) make mach_mpoly leave spurious `-0=0` / `1=-0+1` coefficient leaves. Fix: reduce to the (p,q,s,t)-abstract conjugacy_poly (which normalises cleanly) by first rewriting y-x -> (y-mu)-(x-mu). Same family as the overlapping-atom rule: keep atoms abstract, feed real terms by application.

common_mistakes.tactic: modelling the unconditional MSE as a genuine 2-D integral
common_mistakes.why_fails: MachLib has no 2-D integration and no Fubini. The iterated-integral device avoids it: take the inner x-integral first (closed-form via parallel-axis = tau2+(phi(y)-m(y))^2), leaving a single 1-D outer y-integral. optimalMSE_tendsto and mse_lower_bound are then ordinary 1-D improper-integral facts.

MachLib has no measurable-function type to quantify over. mse_lower_bound is honestly stated for any CONTINUOUS phi:Real->Real (enough to invoke continuous_riemann_integrable + riemann_integral_mono); the conditional posterior_mean_mmse holds for any point estimate c with no regularity at all.
